sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
உமையொரு பங்கன் என்று ஊரெங்கும் பேசிட
தந்தையின் முதுகிலே தழும்பென்ன மாயமம்மா
sections.translit:
umaiyoru pangan endRu Urengum pEsida
thandhaiyin mudhugilE thazhumbenna mAyamammA
sections.en: Oh mother, the whole world is talking about father sharing a part of his body with you. Yet I see a scar on his back. How did this magical bruise happen?

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
அடித்தது யாரென்று அறிந்திலையோ உடனுறைந்தே
தடுத்திலையோ சக்தியை ஓர் கணம் இழந்தனையோ
sections.translit:
aditthadhu yArendRu aRindhilaiyO udanuRaindhE
thadutthilaiyO sakthiyai Or kaNam izhandhanaiyO
sections.en: Did you not know who the offender was? Mother, since you dwell within Him, why didn’t you try to stop him from being hit? Oh Parasakthi, did you momentarily lose your strength and energy?

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
பிட்டுக்கு ஆசை கொண்டே ஐயன் பட்ட துயர் அறிந்தேன்
அடியார்க்கு மண் சுமந்தாரைப் படியார் என்றெண்ணி
தடியால் அடித்ததுவும் தகுமோ மன்னுயிர் நேசர்க்கு
மறுதரம் மாசு நேரிடின் உடனுரைத்திடுவாய் உலகநாயகியே
sections.translit:
pittukku Asai koNdE aiyan patta thuyar aRindhEn
adiyArkku maN sumandhAraip padiyAr endReNNi
thadiyAl aditthadhuvum thagumO mannuyir nEsarkku
maRudharam mAsu nEridin udanuraitthiduvAy ulaganAyakiyE
sections.en: I learnt of the suffering my father went through because of his love for pudding. Is it justified to strike him with a pole without properly inquiring? In fact, my father was simply helping an elderly devotee and doing manual labor on her behalf. Protector of the universe, if this kind of offense or wrongdoing happens again to my father, let me know right away.

notes: This song was written for a dance performance by my daughter, Priti (née) Radhakrishnan, as a fundraiser for the Siva Murugan Temple in Concord, CA. Her Guru, Smt. Mythili Kumar, trained her for this program with original choreography for this song and another “Veedu vittu Odippona vadivelare”. This song, “Umaiyoru pangan”, is based on Thiruvilaiyadal puranam, where Lord Siva had performed magical acts on behalf of the devotees in Madurai. This is a piece written from the poet’s imagination, from the perspective of young Muruga. When he saw a scar on his father’s back and learnt the background story, he was furious and demanded to know why his mother did not stop this. Muruga sarcastically chastises his mother, Parvathi, that following this incident, the protector of the universe should let him handle it if any such incidents occur in his father’s life. Once there was heavy flooding in the Vaigai river and the ruling King, Arimarddhana Pandiyan, mandated that each family should send an able body to help with the creation of a dam, to mitigate the damage from the flood. There was an old lady named Vandhi who used to cook and serve pittu (a sweet dry pudding) to earn a living. She was all alone and had no family to send as an able body. She prayed to Lord Siva to help. Siva descended on earth as a handyman with a spade and a spear and agreed to assist the old lady in exchange for her pittu. After a few hours of working as a handyman, Siva pretended to relax under a tree. The king’s guards found him in that position, loitering. The king rushed to the site and lashed Siva for his arrogant behavior. The scar from the lashes showed up on the backs of all of the world’s creatures. The king realized the worker was none other than Lord Siva. He kneeled and begged for his pardon with tears running down his cheeks. Siva blessed him, while mounted on his bullock with Parvathi seated next to him. For details of the entire episode, see: கூடல் மாநகரத்து ஆடவல்லான் (திருவிளையாடற் புராண மகிமை), நாகர்கோவில் கிருஷ்ணன், முதற் பதிப்பு 2003, Published by Mathi Nilayam. #4 (39) Thanikachalam Road, Brindavan Apartments, T.Nagar, Chennai 600017, Ph: 4311838, Chapter 61. மண் சுமந்த படலம், பக்கம்: 456 – 467. Celebration of Siva’s act of compassion Pittukku maN Sumandha Piran
